title: Verba Deponentia
subtitle: Hortor, sequor, patior — forma passiva, significatio activa.
objectives: Cognoscere verba deponentia: forma passiva, significatio activa
Coniugare deponentia per omnia tempora, in forma passiva
Uti participio perfecto deponenti cum significatione ACTIVA (unica lacuna systematis participiorum sic impleta)

content.intro: 'Deponent' venit ā 'dēpōnō' ('to lay aside') — haec verba dēposuērunt (laid aside) significātiōnem passīvam, retinentēs sōlum fōrmam passīvam cum significātiōne āctīvā.
content.explanation: Verbum dēpōnēns cōniugātur EXACTĒ ut passīvum normāle (amor, amāris, amātur...), sed significat āctīvē: hortor nōn significat 'I am urged' sed 'I urge'.

rules.heading: a) Exempla, Unum per Coniugationem
rules.body:
Coniug.VerbumSignificatio
Ihortor, hortārī, hortātus sumto urge, exhort
IIvereor, verērī, veritus sumto fear
IIIsequor, sequī, secūtus sumto follow
III mixtapatior, patī, passus sumto suffer, allow
IVorior, orīrī, ortus sumto rise, arise

Nōtā: dictiōnārium dat tantum TRĒS fōrmās (nūllum -ō āctīvum, quia nōn exsistit): hortor (praesēns), hortārī (īnfīnītīvus), hortātus sum (perfectum).

rules.heading: b) Coniugatio: Identica Passivo
rules.body: Praesēns: hortor, hortāris, hortātur, hortāmur, hortāminī, hortantur. Imperfectum: hortābar, hortābāris... Futūrum: hortābor, hortāberis... Perfectum: hortātus sum, hortātus es... (participium + sum, ut in passīvō, sed hīc significātiō est ĀCTĪVA).

rules.heading: c) Lacuna Impleta: Participium Perfectum Activum
rules.body: Recorda: Latīna Classica normāliter CARET participiō perfectī āctīvī ('having done', āctīvē). Deponentia SOLA implent hanc lacūnam: secūtus significat 'having followed' (āctīvē!), nōn 'having been followed'. Hostem secūtus, mīles eum cēpit. ('Having followed the enemy, the soldier captured him.')

rules.heading: d) Verba Semi-Deponentia
rules.body: Paucī verba sunt āctīva in systēmate praesentis, sed dēpōnentia in systēmate perfectī: audeō, audēre, ausus sum (to dare), gaudeō, gaudēre, gāvīsus sum (to rejoice), soleō, solēre, solitus sum (to be accustomed).

examples: Dux milites hortatur. — The leader urges the soldiers.
Canis dominum sequitur. — The dog follows its master.
Multa passi sumus. — We have suffered many things.
Hostem secutus, eum cepit. — Having followed the enemy, he captured him.
Id facere ausus est. — He dared to do it. (semi-deponens)

commonMistakes.wrong: 'Hortor' vertitur passivē: 'I am urged', per formam passivam apparentem.
commonMistakes.right: 'Hortor' significat activē: 'I urge' — deponentia SEMPER significant active, quamvis forma sit passiva.
commonMistakes.why: Haec est definitio ipsa 'deponentis': significatio activa, forma passiva, sine exceptione.

commonMistakes.wrong: Participium perfectum deponens ('secutus') vertitur passive: 'having been followed'.
commonMistakes.right: 'secutus' significat active: 'having followed' — unica excepcion ubi Latina habet participium perfectum activum.
commonMistakes.why: Deponentia implent hanc lacunam quam verba normalia implere non possunt.

items.explanation: Unica lacuna impleta: participium perfectum ACTIVUM.

items.prompt: Quot formae principales dantur pro verbo deponenti in dictionario?
items.explanation: hortor, hortari, hortatus sum — tres formae, nullum activum -o exsistit.
Activum in praesenti, deponens in perfecto.
3a persona sg., forma passiva/significatio activa: sequitur.

items.prompt: Multa ___. (we have suffered — passi sumus, pati)

summary: Verba deponentia: forma passiva, significatio activa, semper (hortor = I urge).
Tres formae principales (praesens, infinitivus, perfectum) — nullum -o activum.
Participium perfectum deponens (secutus) est ACTIVUM: 'having followed' — unica lacuna impleta.
Semi-deponentia: activa in praesenti, deponentia in perfecto (audeo, gaudeo, soleo).
